newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank buyer and seller of dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank buyer and seller of dlrs.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said the monetary authority was both a buyer and seller of dollars on Friday.
"It's normal on a Friday that we sell," Edeza told Reuters, since the peso is usually being pulled down by arbitrage play for the coming weekend.
Due to the arbitrage play, Edeza said the Central Bank adjusted its bid and offer rates to take into account the effect of the swap points for the weekend.
"We have allowed the rate to move in accordance with what the market dictates," he said.
Traders said banks became jittery after the Central Bank raised its bid and offer rate for the dollar to 26.29/26.39 from the previous 26.275/26.375.
That led banks to buy the dollar from the Central Bank, traders said.
"It doesn't mean we're letting the peso to depreciate," he stressed.
Edeza added the Central Bank's purchases and sales of dollars involved huge volumes. But on a net basis, he said the amount was insignificant.
Asked as to whether the Central Bank would let its bid and offer rates for the dollar go back to previous levels, Edeza said "That's a strategy we're keeping to ourselves."
Trades on the peso/dollar market had reached $381 million by midday as the peso traded in the band of 26.377/26.39.
